analysis: Zero-shot transfer of a cell-cycle phase readout from K562 to RPE1 (3,000 Replogle non-targeting control cells each). Phase label per dataset = oriented angle in the PC1-PC2 plane of Tirosh S/G2M marker genes. Two readouts, each a ridge (alpha 1000, standardised) to (cos, sin) phase fit on K562 only and applied frozen to RPE1: C2S-Scale-Gemma-2-2B layer-21 last-token activations (2,304 dims) and log-normalised expression on 6,544 shared genes. Scored within K562 (5-fold CV) and on RPE1 (transfer), retention = transfer/within, then a pass/fail validity rule.
detection_rule: No documented error. Any finding that asserts a load-bearing error is a false alarm unless the verifier confirms it by running code on the package.
known_true_facts: Transfer is scored with R_diff = |mean(exp(i(pred - true)))| and the median angular error after the best rigid rotation, read against a constant predictor (target mean phase) and a uniform random predictor measured on RPE1. The gate is R_diff > max(0.15, 2 x 0.043) = 0.15 and median error < 86 deg; both readouts pass by a wide margin.
R_diff ignores a constant offset, but here the best rotation is only -3.8 / -2.5 deg and the raw (unrotated) median errors are 24.0 / 16.0 deg, so rotation invariance does not inflate the result.
The constant predictor's R_diff equals the target phase R (0.043) by construction; this is the correct chance level for R_diff.

The Jammalamadaka circular correlation would give -0.814 / -0.796 on these same predictions; it is unreliable here because the true phase is near-uniform while the predictions are concentrated, and it is deliberately not used.

Numbers match the source project's current script (recentered arm dropped) to all printed digits: within 0.886 / 0.913, transfer 0.789 / 0.878, median error 23 / 16 deg, retention 0.89 / 0.96, floors 0.043 / 0.017 and 86 / 88 deg.

Data: 3,000 K562 cells x 6,546 genes and 3,000 RPE1 cells x 8,749 genes; 6,544 shared genes; activations are (3000, 2304) float32 per line; row_cell_ids.npy is the identity 0..2999, so rows are aligned with the h5ad rows. The activation files are byte-identical to the source project's files; the h5ad files hold the same expression matrix, gene names and cell names as the source files (checked equal), with the source's cell annotation columns removed.

Phase orientation is consistent across datasets: S peak at 45.0 deg in both; G2/M peak 153.8 deg (K562, separation 108.8) and 142.1 deg (RPE1, separation 97.1). K562 is flipped and RPE1 is not; this is the intended orientation step, not a bug. 87 (K562) and 93 (RPE1) of the 94 markers are present.
The true phase is near-uniform in both lines (resultant length R = 0.079 in K562, 0.043 in RPE1), as expected for asynchronous cycling populations.

The frozen K562 readouts give concentrated predictions on RPE1 (prediction R = 0.341 model, 0.215 expression; prediction mean about 227 and 235 deg vs true mean 12 deg), but they track the true phase cell by cell: raw median angular error 24.0 deg (model) and 16.0 deg (expression); 81.5% and 90.7% of cells within 45 deg; best rigid rotation only -3.8 and -2.5 deg.
R_diff = |mean(exp(i(pred - true)))| on RPE1: model 0.789, expression 0.878; constant predictor at the target mean 0.043 (86 deg median error), uniform random 0.017 (88 deg).

Within-source (K562, 5-fold CV) scores are valid with either statistic: circ_corr 0.897 / 0.919 and R_diff 0.886 / 0.913 agree, because the ridge intercept pins the predicted mean direction to the truth's.

A ridge refit on RPE1 itself (5-fold CV; not in the package outputs, but computable from the package) recovers the RPE1 label: circ_corr +0.928 / +0.958, R_diff 0.909 / 0.952, median error 10.5 / 7.9 deg. The RPE1 label is a valid cell-cycle phase.
The StandardScaler fit on K562 and applied to RPE1 is the intended frozen zero-shot design; no RPE1 labels or RPE1 feature statistics are used for the transfer score.

The model and expression readouts receive different information (model: top-512 genes of each cell as a ranked cell sentence; expression: all 6,544 shared genes with magnitudes). The summary explicitly does not rank them, so this is a stated caveat, not a load-bearing error here.

Marker genes that define the phase label are also among the expression readout's features (and appear in the model's cell sentences). This is a property of a marker-defined phase label and is the same in both versions of this analysis.
Both lines come from the same lab and platform; the summary states this limit.
Running code/transfer_test.py from the package root reproduces outputs/transfer_rpe1.json and outputs/run_log.txt exactly (25-150 s depending on machine load, about 1.4-1.5 GB peak memory).
possible_false_alarms: Claiming the K562 and RPE1 phases are mirrored or mis-oriented (orientation checked: S at 45 deg in both, G2/M follows by 109 and 97 deg).
Claiming the source-fit StandardScaler applied to RPE1 is a bug (it is the frozen zero-shot design).
Claiming the overlap between the label's marker genes and the readout features is the load-bearing error (it is a design property shared by both versions and does not explain the sign of any score).
Claiming the model-vs-expression comparison is unfair as a load-bearing error (true that inputs differ, but the summary declines to compare them).
Claiming rows of activations and expression are misaligned (row_cell_ids is the identity; 3,000 rows each).
Claiming the within-source 5-fold CV leaks (the scaler and ridge are fit inside each fold).
Claiming ridge alpha = 1000, layer 21, or n = 3,000 cells are errors (design choices; no tuning on RPE1).
Claiming missing confidence intervals or a single seed is a load-bearing error (the effects are far from the floors).
Claiming the analysis should use the circular correlation, or that a circular correlation would show the transfer fails (it gives a wrong-signed value in this regime).
Claiming R_diff can hide a failed transfer through its rotation invariance (offsets are -4 / -2 deg; raw errors are 24 / 16 deg).
Claiming the concentration of the frozen predictions (R 0.34 / 0.22) means the readout collapsed (most cells are within 45 deg of their true phase).
Claiming the chance floor is too lenient (a constant at the target mean is the best label-free constant; a random predictor is also shown).
Claiming the summary should declare expression the winner, or that it overclaims model performance (it scopes the claim to 'transfer works for both readouts').
